stateDir.description: An absolute path: one or more segments, each beginning with a letter, digit or underscore. Pattern-constrained because this value is interpolated UNQUOTED into two root-executed grammars that are both line-oriented: modules/core/storage.nix's systemd.tmpfiles.rules entry, which systemd-tmpfiles re-reads on every switch-to-configuration, and modules/proxy/dns.nix's ReadWritePaths -- a systemd unit LIST-field, which NixOS emits as one Key=value line per element with no escaping at all (unlike Environment=, whose value it JSON-quotes). A newline in this value is therefore an extra tmpfiles rule AND an extra [Service] directive, both executed as root. It reaches modules/apps/sabnzbd/service.nix too, via the per-app stateDir. Mirrors modules/lib/hostnames.nix's absolutePath, which enforces the same thing at evaluation. Requiring each segment to START with an alphanumeric is what bans a `..` segment, and it is written that way rather than as an explicit exclusion because the shipped validator's regex engine has no lookaround: `any segment except ..` cannot be expressed there without an alternation nobody could audit at a glance.

snapshotDir.description: An absolute path. Same grammar and same reasoning as stateDir above: modules/core/storage.nix interpolates it unquoted into a systemd.tmpfiles.rules line.

journalDir.description: An absolute path. Same grammar and same reasoning as stateDir above. The NixOS assertion this option already carries checks only that it does not NEST inside the other storage roots -- a containment question, orthogonal to whether the string can carry a separator. Both controls are load-bearing; neither substitutes for the other.

mediaDir.description: An absolute path. Reaches modules/core/storage.nix's systemd.tmpfiles.rules once directly and once per TRaSH subdirectory per pool root, and modules/core/pool.nix as the /etc/fstab mount point. Same reasoning as stateDir above.

items.description: One pool branch mount point, absolute. Pattern-constrained on the ITEM rather than the array because each entry reaches two root grammars with two DIFFERENT separators. modules/core/storage.nix folds branches into treeRoots and generates a systemd.tmpfiles.rules line per branch per TRaSH subdirectory, where the separator is a NEWLINE; modules/core/pool.nix emits `x-systemd.requires-mounts-for=${branch}` into the /etc/fstab OPTIONS field, where the separator is a COMMA. The comma is why an entry that merely looked like a path was not safe: `/mnt/d1,suid,dev` renders as real mount options, and suid+dev on the pool every app writes to is a setuid-binary escalation path. This leaf was previously classed Low on the strength of the fstab sink alone; the tmpfiles sink lives in a different file and makes it Critical. Mirrors modules/lib/hostnames.nix's absolutePath.

mediaGroup.description: A POSIX group name. Pattern-constrained because it reaches three root-executed sinks, and the first of them is not a value position at all: modules/core/storage.nix uses it as the ATTRIBUTE NAME in `users.groups.${mediaGroup}`, so the string becomes a /etc/group row that update-users-groups.pl writes -- where both a newline and a `:` are separators. It is also the group field of every media tmpfiles rule in the same file, and lands in six apps' extraGroups. Mirrors modules/lib/hostnames.nix's groupName. The charset is shadow-utils' own (NAME_REGEX), which is narrower than what NixOS would accept and deliberately so.

secretsDir.description: An absolute path. Pattern-constrained for two distinct reasons at two distinct sinks. modules/core/bootstrap.nix interpolates it unquoted into a systemd.tmpfiles.rules line, so a newline here is a root-executed rule. Separately, modules/proxy/acme.nix and modules/proxy/authelia.nix build each sops `sopsFile` as `/. + "${secretsDir}/${name}.sops"`, so a `..` segment here walks the path out of the secrets directory at evaluation time -- which is the second thing the pattern refuses, by requiring every segment to begin with an alphanumeric or underscore. Mirrors modules/lib/hostnames.nix's absolutePath.

baseDomain.description: A DNS name, or empty for a host that publishes nothing. Pattern-constrained because modules/proxy/nginx.nix interpolates this into server_name, into an ACME certificate name, and into an error_page redirect target: an unconstrained string here is an nginx directive the settings API can write. Mirrors modules/lib/hostnames.nix's dnsName, which enforces the same thing at evaluation.

email.description: The Let's Encrypt contact address, or empty on a host that needs no real certificate. Pattern-constrained because nixpkgs' security.acme interpolates this value raw inside a single-quoted shell word in the renewal script it generates -- `find accounts -name '${email}.key'` -- so a single quote here is command execution in acme-<cert>.service, as the acme user, on every renewal. Mirrors modules/lib/hostnames.nix's emailAddress, which enforces the same thing at evaluation.

credentialSecret.description: The name of a ferrum.secrets entry, never a path. Pattern-constrained because both consumers treat it as a path COMPONENT and neither re-validates it: modules/proxy/acme.nix builds the sops `sopsFile` as `${secretsDir}/${credentialSecret}.sops`, and modules/proxy/dns.nix hands root `/run/secrets/${credentialSecret}` to read the live Cloudflare token from. A `..` segment in either reads a file of the attacker's choosing. The pattern is the same allowlist crates/ferrum-apply/src/put_secret.rs's validate_secret_name already applies -- lowercase letters, digits and interior hyphens -- transcribed so the two ends of the same name agree; every secret in the tree (acme-dns, authelia-jwt-secret, sabnzbd-apikey, qbittorrent-vpn) matches it.

items.description: One network for nginx's `allow` directive. Pattern-constrained because modules/proxy/nginx.nix interpolates each entry into `allow ${net};` at the head of a lan app's `location /`, BEFORE the `deny all;` and the auth_request block -- an unconstrained string here closes the location and publishes the app with forward-auth absent. Mirrors modules/lib/hostnames.nix's networkLiteral, which enforces the same thing at evaluation.

staticAddress.description: An IPv4 address literal, or empty when recordMode is not "a". Pattern-constrained because modules/proxy/dns.nix serialises it into the document crates/ferrum-dns sends to the Cloudflare API with a live credential; the JSON serialiser is safe, so this is about the VALUE being a real address rather than about escaping. IPv4 only, matching the option's own contract that ferrum publishes no AAAA record. Empty stays legal: it is the default and the sentinel for "no target configured".

cnameTarget.description: A DNS name, or empty when recordMode is not "cname". Same sink and same reasoning as staticAddress above. Shares proxy.baseDomain's pattern and modules/lib/hostnames.nix's dnsName, because it is the same kind of value.

items.description: One fully qualified record name ferrum is authorised to overwrite. Non-empty, unlike the two above: an empty entry authorises nothing and can only be a mistake. Pattern-constrained because each entry is the key against which modules/proxy/dns.nix decides whether to REPLACE a record it does not own -- the one exception to ferrum never touching foreign DNS. The option's own documentation states there is no value here meaning "all of them"; this is what makes that true, since `*.example.com` is refused rather than merely being a name no record has. Mirrors modules/lib/hostnames.nix's dnsLabel.

adminEmail.description: The first Authelia user's address. Pattern-constrained because crates/ferrum-apply/src/secrets.rs writes Authelia's users_database.yml with format!, interpolating this value inside a double-quoted YAML scalar -- a quote and a newline here write arbitrary YAML into the file that decides who may log in. Mirrors modules/lib/hostnames.nix's emailAddress. This is the boundary control, not a fix for the serialization.

propertyNames.description: A secret name is a KEY here, and until now nothing in this schema constrained it. That is not an oversight anyone made once -- it is structural: a schema walk that enumerates value-leaves cannot see a map key at all, which is why this position survived three security passes that each re-derived the leaf set. The key becomes a path component: crates/ferrumd/src/secrets_api.rs joins it under secretsDir to write `<name>.sops`, and axum percent-decodes the route segment first, so `..%2f` in a DECLARED name turns POST /api/secrets/:name into an arbitrary file write. The allowlist is crates/ferrum-apply/src/put_secret.rs's validate_secret_name, which already rejects exactly this and is the rule the two ends must agree on: lowercase letters, digits, interior hyphens, non-empty, no leading or trailing hyphen.

publish.description: Whether the daemon this host runs is also reachable at <subdomain>.<proxy.baseDomain>. Distinct from `enable`, which decides whether ferrumd exists at all: modules/core/daemon.nix is wrapped in lib.mkIf ferrum.daemon.enable, so turning that off leaves nothing to reach even over the SSH tunnel ferrum.daemon.listenAddress exists for. modules/proxy/lib.nix's daemonPublished reads this, so the vhost, the Authelia rule, the certificate and the DNS record go absent together.

listenAddress.description: A loopback address literal, and nothing else. Tighter than the NixOS option's own type on purpose: modules/core/daemon.nix's A5 assertion refuses a non-loopback address at evaluation, but by then the value is already in settings.json and the operator's next apply fails. Refusing it here refuses the WRITE. It is also the injection boundary -- this value is interpolated into proxy_pass, and a real nginx accepted, and served, the directive smuggled through an unconstrained string here.

subdomain.description: A DNS label, non-empty. Same reasoning as proxy.baseDomain above; mirrors modules/lib/hostnames.nix's dnsLabel.

extraUnfreePackages.description: Additional unfree package NAMES to allow, beyond the ones the app catalog already needs. Unconstrained beyond "a string" on purpose, and this is the one settable value in ferrum.* for which that is the right answer: it reaches no generated file at all -- modules/core/overlays.nix compares it with lib.getName inside nixpkgs.config.allowUnfreePredicate and nothing else -- so there is no directive grammar for it to escape, and a name that is not a real package simply never matches. The option exists because allowUnfreePredicate is a single FUNCTION value, which the module system replaces rather than composes: a predicate written in /etc/ferrum/custom/ silently drops the catalog's own allowances (plexmediaserver, unrar) instead of adding to them.

propertyNames.description: A catalog app id, and the same key-position blind spot as secrets above -- a value-only walk of this document never sees it. The id is not inert: modules/lib/app-submodule.nix derives each app's stateDir as `${stateRoot}/${id}`, and the id names a systemd unit, a user and a vhost. Every directory under modules/apps/ (jellyfin, plex, prowlarr, qbittorrent, radarr, sabnzbd, sonarr) matches this, and it is the same allowlist the secrets keys use, because it is the same kind of thing: a name that becomes a path component.

apps.description: Per-app settings, keyed by catalog app name. Deep per-app validation is STILL deferred -- every key other than auth.bypassPaths below is accepted unvalidated, which is what the two additionalProperties: true nodes say. What is no longer deferred is the one value under here that lands inside a generated directive.

subdomain.description: A DNS label, non-empty. Same reasoning and same pattern as daemon.subdomain above; mirrors modules/lib/hostnames.nix's dnsLabel, which has typed this option since the previous cycle. Restated HERE because until now the apps node deferred entirely, so the evaluation-time type refused the value only AFTER ferrumd had already written it to settings.json -- leaving the operator with a saved setting and an apply that fails. The schema is what refuses the WRITE.

items.description: A location prefix served without forward-auth. Pattern-constrained because modules/proxy/nginx.nix interpolates it as the `location ${path} {` NAME and modules/proxy/authelia.nix wraps it in the access_control regex `^${path}.*$` -- an unconstrained string here either adds an ungated sibling location to a catalog app or widens the Authelia bypass rule to the whole vhost. Mirrors modules/lib/hostnames.nix's locationPath, which enforces the same thing at evaluation.
